a.text: You should all bless me. Bless me with a dance under the morning sun and the tapping of your scabbards.
—Oh, right, I forgot you sold your swords. Then beat the pots and pans. Play the anvil like a drum with your pens.
They say the roads of Menat-Ha'mait are paved with jewels. Well, I'm heading for that road now.
I know most of you will tell me to stop being delusional. But why can't I make it rich?
Why can't I buy us the best life?

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: Where am I—?

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: —Oh, my departure ceremony! I must have danced myself dizzy.

steps.name: Cheerful Former Desert Bandit
steps.text: I give you my blessing, Narantuya.

steps.name: Cheerful Former Desert Bandit
steps.text: There's a caravan I know that regularly visits the City of Radiance. If you do make it there, seek them out.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: Hah, I knew you'd have some useful connections!

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: One more friend, one less trouble. Thanks for the blessing.

steps.name: Doubtful Former Desert Bandit
steps.text: I'm still worried, Narantuya.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: About what? How many times have I told you? No one's going to get revenge on you when I'm gone.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: This has nothing to do with you. You chose to work for me and not Asim because I'm just that charming.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: Old Asim resents me for it and speaks ill of me everywhere he goes, but he's just being petty.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: And those jealous haters had to band together and set me up... my fault I'm so lucky that I attract both gold and people.

steps.name: Doubtful Former Desert Bandit
steps.text: But you're the one I'm worried about, Narantuya.

steps.name: Doubtful Former Desert Bandit
steps.text: if you just wander into the desert with an empty satchel, what will you do when you can't find water or beasts?

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: Huh? I know we somehow ended up poorer than we started, but I'm sure I at least have some coins for jerkies and preserved fruits.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: Why would you think that? Has anyone been starving without telling me? Who is it?

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: I'll give them some coins right now—
Narantuya reaches into the purse at her waist.
As her eyes slowly widen in disbelief, she unties the beast hide pouch, turns it inside out, and begins shaking it.
A few grains of sand fall onto the endless desert.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: Strange. I don't remember bumping into a beggar or vagrant...

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: Actually, I vaguely remember crossing paths with a few rich men?

steps.name: Doubtful Former Desert Bandit
steps.text: Narantuya, I thought it over, and I think I should teach you my secret to finding water in the desert.

steps.name: Doubtful Former Desert Bandit
steps.text: I don't have to worry about becoming a sacrificial tribute to a bandit chief anymore, so there's no need to keep this a secret any longer.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: —Good. I like this blessing.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: The sands can enjoy those lost coins then.

steps.name: Ajazi
steps.text: I'm worried too, Narantuya.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: Hmm? And what are you worried about? That I'll abduct another child slave from a caravan who will replace you as most illiterate?

spans.text: worried about? That I'll abduct another child slave from a caravan who will replace you as most illiterate?

steps.name: Ajazi
steps.text: I'm worried about the two black blades of yours. You haven't used or maintained them for a long time.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: It's precisely because maintenance is a chore that I avoid using these antiques. I much prefer modern materials and mechanical forging—

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: —Wait, where are my blades? And my dagger? And my supply of paralyzing toxins and spore casks?

steps.name: Ajani
steps.text: *sigh* I'm worried about your tendency to pick up new recruits, Narantuya.

steps.name: Ajani
steps.text: You'll be setting out alone. It's great if you could get some useful crew. But most of the time, it's people like me and Ajazi that you have to save...

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: 'Setting out alone'? You girls aren't coming with me to the City of Radiance?

steps.name: Ajani
steps.text: ...which is why Ajazi and I worked for two months in a logging camp and threw all the coins we saved into a river they say flows into the City of Radiance.

steps.name: Ajani
steps.text: I hope you will find them when the river floods, and that your Khaganquest goes smoothly...

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: Okay, I appreciate this blessing too, even though the rainforest is at the downstream of the river.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: ...Wait.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: Did you say Khaganquest?

steps.name: Ajazi
steps.text: Yes, your Khaganquest.

steps.name: Ajani
steps.text: You're all set for it, right?

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: No? When did that happen?

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: ...Come to think of it, I am indeed 'all by myself with nothing but the weapons from my parents' right now...

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: ...Meh, pass on the city. I'm out!
The young Nightzmora turns and strides over to her burdenbeast pack.
At that same moment, towering walls rise up from the sand. Even part of the piercing sunlight seems to be blocked off.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: Where are my burdenbeasts? And my tent?
Narantuya rubs her eyes.
As if trapped in a nightmare of her own making, her field of vision narrows until only one path remains.

a.text: 'Step forth, prove your bravery, embark on your Khaganquest.'

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: No way! This Khaganquest is too scary! I'll die!

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: Help——!!!

steps.name: Aspasia
steps.text: Strange. The metal constructs here are not moving.

steps.name: Aspasia
steps.text: Someone's on the ground? Hello, can you hear me? Hold on, I'm on my way—

steps.name: Aspasia
steps.text: ——Out of my way!

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: What did you say?

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: I was just lying on the ground and a giant beckbeast had its paw on my head?

steps.name: Aspasia
steps.text: I think it's a beckbeast, but I failed to catch the creature before it vanished into the sand and dust.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: It's no wonder my head hurt while I was dreaming. There was a voice I heard making 'oowoo...' sounds. My face is fine though, right?

steps.name: Aspasia
steps.text: ...Yes.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: Phew.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: How did you chase the beckbeast away? I spent so long yelling at it in my dream with no luck.

steps.name: Aspasia
steps.text: The situation was urgent, so I resorted to force.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: Wow, why didn't I think of that? Sometimes violence is the solution!

spans.text: Wow, why didn't I think of that? Sometimes violence

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: I knew you'd be a reliable subordinate. Thanks a lot—

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: Wait no, you're not a subordinate.

steps.name: Aspasia
steps.text: ...We'd best be leaving. These constructs could start moving at any time. It's not safe here.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: Seems pretty safe to me.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: *sigh* The river god presented me with a chance to prove my heroism, and I ended up falling asleep on the street...?

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: The dream was nice though, at least the first half of it.

steps.name: Aspasia
steps.text: ...The streets are in chaos, while you lay on the sands... and had a good dream?

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: Yup. I dreamed about my departure ceremony. Everyone was cheering me on. Even their beat was spot on.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: How nice would it be, if my former subordinates were actually that supportive when I was setting out for Menat-Ha'mait!

steps.name: Aspasia
steps.text: I talked to Ajazi and Ajani briefly, after you left the hotel.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: Did they tell you most people think I'm delusional?

steps.name: Aspasia
steps.text: They did.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: But consider this: if one has to eventually wake from one's dream, why not indulge in a bit of fantasy before that happens?

steps.name: Aspasia
steps.text: (Can't help but laugh)

steps.name: Aspasia
steps.text: Perhaps there remains much of each other that we do not know.

steps.name: Aspasia
steps.text: But for now, I'm simply glad to see you safe.
Aspasia extends her hand to Narantuya.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: So, does that mean we're all good—

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: —Hold on.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: What's wrong, Ajani?

steps.name: Ajani
steps.text: Narantuya! Help!

steps.name: Ajani
steps.text: The museum! Isn't safe! At all!

steps.name: Anat
steps.text: —Who's there?

steps.name: Anat
steps.text: Titi, did you say something? I heard something...

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: I didn't.

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: ...But I heard it too.

steps.name: Anat
steps.text: Uh, no way...

steps.name: Anat
steps.text: Can these artifacts talk?

steps.name: Anat
steps.text: Ugh... Why didn't they say anything before?!

steps.name: Jewel Construct
steps.text: Guardian of eternity. Please answer. Please answer. Please answer.

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: Answer what?

steps.name: Jewel Construct
steps.text: He who led the outlanders to stride upon the earth, forsaking their ships from this domain. His legions, brandishing golden blades, shielded the reckless and inquisitive travelers.

steps.name: Jewel Construct
steps.text: Bitter and sweet, his chalice did contain, drawn from those who traversed through his realm. In the sands beneath his feet, rest bones and charred stones from the distant northwest.

steps.name: Jewel Construct
steps.text: Tell me, the 'name' that people remember him by.

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: ...Anat.

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: I don't think they can actually 'talk', at least, they're not capable of conversation.

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: They're just presenting riddles—like when you're prompted to enter a combination of numbers to open a safe.

steps.name: Anat
steps.text: B-But! What kind of complex riddle is this?!

steps.name: Jewel Construct
steps.text: The countdown has begun. Three minutes remaining.

steps.name: Anat
steps.text: Ahhhhh!!!

steps.name: Anat
steps.text: Now we've turned it into a ticking time bomb!

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: —Wait, Anat! Calm down!

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: Can you contact any of the museum staff?

steps.name: Anat
steps.text: Wh-What for...?

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: I think this might be a riddle about history.

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: I remember now... what about that favorite book of yours, Terra: A Journey? Where is it?

spans.text: I remember now... what about that favorite book of yours,

steps.name: Anat
steps.text: Titi, look up the section on Bolívar's history for me, please!

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: Here.

steps.name: Anat
steps.text: ...You ask of Padishah Beyad, who agreed to establish an Iberia-Sargon-Bolívar trade route and subsequently brought in Bolívarian sugar cane and coffee beans.

steps.name: Anat
steps.text: 'Corrupted by the land's blight, tiny skulls strung on leather tight. Clanking with agony, from their plight. Hunted they are, day and night...'

steps.name: Anat
steps.text: I know! Chapter three, beasts of Terra.

steps.name: Anat
steps.text: You ask of sandbeast. There was a trend in sixth-century Sargon to hunt sandbeasts.

steps.name: Anat
steps.text: The museum used to have strings of sandbeast heads hung up to ward off evil, though we always saw it as a needless worship of nature.

steps.name: Anat
steps.text: But... since you've witnessed that history. You should know that the real reason for hunting sandbeasts was that a small number of them mutated from high concentration of local active Originium, right?

steps.name: Anat
steps.text: Okay, next construct and riddle, please.

steps.name: Anat
steps.text: 'At the lake's bottom, their ruins dwell. Heirs of an old bloodline, many fell. Executed with blades that gleamed. They turned on their own, it seemed...'

steps.name: Anat
steps.text: I remember this one. Go to the end of the races of Terra.

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: A riddle suited for archaeologists. There was an ancient settlement from a thousand years ago where we found signs of group executions, but we excavated torture instruments made of modern alloy materials.

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: You're right, the answer is written here. Petram, a race practically no one has seen, are those who inherited unique smelting and forging techniques from the olden times

steps.name: Anat
steps.text: Okay, next question...
The constructs' riddles are solved as the pages turn, and they gradually settle down.
They stop in a circle around Anat, like a group of silent listeners.
Anat recalls the moment right before she gave her first speech. Titi taught her to imagine the audience as museum artifacts to calm her nerves.
'Just keep talking about the things you know are true, Anat.'

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: Phew, this is taboo to say, but the Sarkaz did indeed set foot in Sargon once. We still don't know the full extent of their ancient curse.

steps.name: Anat
steps.text: Come to think of it, this is how you've inspired me.

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: Huh? You mean the curse?

steps.name: Anat
steps.text: No. I used to not get it.

steps.name: Anat
steps.text: Sargon's written history dates back to when other nations were still in their primitive states. When you left Sargon to explore these lands, I wondered what more you hoped to learn.

steps.name: Anat
steps.text: That's why I chose to read Terra: A Journey.

spans.text: That's why I chose to read

steps.name: Anat
steps.text: I saw within our limited time on this land that we hold too many misunderstandings and prejudices.

steps.name: Anat
steps.text: The greatest show of bravery we can perform is to expend our finite lives on our search through the infinity of time.

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: Yeah, we're no actual guardians of eternity, so there's no way we can experience everything ourselves.

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: Speaking of which, if you ever got the chance... would you become an immortal like Zubayr, and witness ancient history with your own eyes?

steps.name: Anat
steps.text: Actually, I've been thinking... if these constructs are using history riddles to verify if we are worthy of controlling them...

steps.name: Anat
steps.text: Then what was the word that activated this verification mode of theirs?

steps.name: Anat
steps.text: And what exactly was their creator thinking when they chose this command word—'Horakhet'?

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: It's dark... Where am I?

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: I'm... in that monster's belly...

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: I can hear the wind...

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Phew... what's up ahead...?

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: A lake in the desert...?
An emerald lake lies in the center of the golden sands. The palm trees by its shore sway in the gentle breeze, creating the rustling sound Pepe heard earlier.
A boy is half submerged in the water. After a moment, he suddenly sits up with a beautiful golden fin in hand.
He holds the fin with both hands, and carefully makes his way towards Pepe.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Uh, kid, do you know...?

steps.name: Young Boy
steps.text: Look at my catch, sister!

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Sister? Who're you calling sister?

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: What... are you talking about?

steps.name: Young Boy
steps.text: Father says he plans to bury Mother here, in her hometown.

steps.name: Young Boy
steps.text: He also wants to erect a beautiful tomb for her, with a pretty pond full of lotuses.

steps.name: Young Boy
steps.text: I will leave this golden fin in that pond, and it will keep Mother company for me.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: What's that got to do with me?

steps.name: Young Boy
steps.text: Sister...

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Stop calling me that! You don't look anything like my brother!

steps.name: Young Boy
steps.text: Father... will continue with his expedition. Mother's departure will not stop him.

steps.name: Young Boy
steps.text: He asked us if we wished to stay here or follow him eastward.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Um... what are you talking about, boy? I can't make sense of what you're saying.

steps.name: Young Boy
steps.text: I wish to follow Father to the east, to see and conquer lands farther away than here.

steps.name: Young Boy
steps.text: Come with me, sister. Bring your reed pen and papyrus, you will see many sights worth recording, and I shall accomplish great undertakings, as Father has.

steps.name: Young Boy
steps.text: I will become the protagonist of your writings!

steps.name: Young Boy
steps.text: Let's go together, sister!

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Hey, li'l guy, I'll have to pass...

steps.name: Gentle Girl
steps.text: Hm...

steps.name: Gentle Girl
steps.text: I'll follow you and Father, Zubayr.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Who...?
Pepe turns her head and sees a girl holding a white lotus, with a similar golden lotus on her forehead, sparkling in the sun.
The decoration reminds Pepe of something, and she lightly touches her own head.
At that moment, the sun seems to make her head spin.
